7499184435393609728.text:
Jane Street tested Etched's hardware, took delivery of the first rack, then led the round that doubled the company to $21B. It was already on the cap table before any of that happened.

$10.3B on July 23. $21B on August 18. A 104% step-up in 26 days, on total funding of $1.9B and one named customer.

That customer is the lead investor. Jane Street was reported as an Etched backer in June, alongside Hudson River Trading, Jump Trading and Two Sigma. The first production rack went to the firm that priced the round. Etched cites $1B+ in customer contracts across frontier labs and clouds, none of them named, and no independent benchmark has cleared the performance claims yet.

7499190915572625408.author: Founderscrowd
7499190915572625408.text:
Etched doubled to $21 billion in a month. Its chip runs one kind of model and nothing else.

Most AI chips are general, ready for whatever architecture wins next. Etched bet the whole company that the transformer is here to stay, and burned that into silicon.

The reward for being right is enormous. A transformer-only chip is far faster and cheaper than one keeping its options open.

The risk is the same size. If the field moves past the transformer, a general chip adapts. This one is scrap.

Jane Street led the round and is also the customer, running the racks.

You trade flexibility for performance and pray the ground does not move.
